Which Azure service stores, versions, and manages private container images?
column2: Azure Container Registry (ACR). Images are addressed as <registry>.azurecr.io/<repo>:<tag>; use unique tags per build (avoid mutable latest in production).

column1: What does ACR Tasks do and what is the key CLI command?
column2: Cloud-based image building/patching in ACR without a local Docker daemon. Key command: az acr build -r <registry> -t <image>:<tag> . — sends context to ACR and builds remotely.

column1: Which ACR Task triggers should you know for the exam?
column2: Commit-triggered builds (source repo webhook), base-image-update triggers (rebuild when the base image is patched), and scheduled tasks. Base-image update is the classic exam answer for "auto-patch containers".

column1: How do you deploy a container to Azure App Service and control the port it listens on?
column2: Point the app at the image (ACR or other registry); App Service injects config as environment variables. If the container listens on a non-80/8080 port, set the WEBSITES_PORT app setting.

column1: How do you supply secrets to an App Service container without hardcoding?
column2: Use app settings (injected as env vars) with Key Vault references (@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=...)), so the app reads the secret value at runtime from Key Vault.

column1: Azure Container Apps: what is an "environment"?
column2: A secure boundary around a group of Container Apps sharing the same virtual network and logging destination. Apps in one environment can talk to each other; it's the deployment scope for an app.

column1: Container Apps revisions — single vs multiple mode?
column2: Single: one active revision at a time (new revision replaces old). Multiple: several revisions active simultaneously with traffic splitting by percentage — used for blue/green and canary. Revisions are immutable snapshots.

column1: What triggers creation of a new Container Apps revision?
column2: Changes to the revision-scope properties: container image, env vars, secrets, scaling rules. A revision name suffix can be set to label it (e.g. --revision-suffix).

column1: What is KEDA and how does it scale Container Apps?
column2: Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling. Scalers poll an external source (Service Bus queue length, Redis list, cron, HTTP) and scale replicas between minReplicas and maxReplicas — including scale to zero when idle.

column1: Exam scenario: a queue-processing Container App must scale with backlog and cost nothing when idle. Answer?
column2: KEDA with a Service Bus queue scaler, minReplicas: 0, and maxReplicas set to the throughput ceiling. Scale rule: message count per replica.

column1: How do you deploy an application to AKS "using manifest files" (the exam phrasing)?
column2: Write YAML manifests (Deployment + Service minimum) and run kubectl apply -f <file.yaml>. Declarative apply is idempotent — re-running converges cluster state to the manifest.

column1: Kubernetes: Deployment vs Service?
column2: Deployment manages replica Pods (rolling updates, rollbacks, self-healing). Service gives a stable virtual IP/DNS name and load-balances across the Pods selected by label.

column1: Kubernetes probe types and what each failure does?
column2: Liveness — failure restarts the container. Readiness — failure removes the Pod from Service endpoints (no traffic) but doesn't restart. Startup — disables liveness/readiness until a slow-starting app is up.

column1: Why set resource requests and limits in a Pod spec?
column2: Requests drive scheduling (node must have that much free CPU/memory) and QoS; limits cap usage — CPU gets throttled, memory over-limit gets the container OOMKilled.

column1: First three kubectl commands when a Pod is failing on AKS?
column2: kubectl get pods (status/restarts) → kubectl describe pod <name> (events: pull failures, probe failures, OOM) → kubectl logs <pod> [-c container] [--previous] (app output, previous crashed container).

column1: How do you inspect cluster-level events and node health on AKS?
column2: kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp for recent warnings; kubectl get nodes and kubectl describe node for pressure conditions (MemoryPressure, DiskPressure).

column1: Exam scenario: AKS Pod is CrashLoopBackOff. Diagnosis path?
column2: kubectl logs --previous for the crash reason, describe pod for exit code (137 = OOM, 1 = app error). CrashLoopBackOff itself just means: keep restarting a container that keeps exiting.

column1: Exam scenario: image won't pull on AKS (ImagePullBackOff). Likely causes?
column2: Wrong image name/tag, registry auth failure (missing/expired imagePullSecret or ACR integration), or network egress blocked. kubectl describe pod shows the exact pull error.

column1: How do you monitor AKS and Container Apps "end-to-end" per the study guide?
column2: Container insights / Azure Monitor for AKS (metrics + logs to Log Analytics), kubectl logs/events for live debugging, and Application Insights/OpenTelemetry for app-level distributed tracing across services.

column1: Container Apps vs AKS — when does the exam want which?
column2: Container Apps: serverless containers, KEDA scaling, revisions, no cluster management. AKS: full Kubernetes control — custom operators, node pools, advanced networking, existing manifests. If the question mentions KEDA/revisions → Container Apps; raw manifests/node config → AKS.

column1: Exam scenario: "build images in CI without Docker installed on the agent"?
column2: ACR Tasks: az acr build builds in Azure from source context; no local daemon needed.

column1: Cosmos DB for NoSQL: how do you connect with the Python SDK?
column2: CosmosClient(endpoint, credential) from azure-cosmos → get_database_client() → get_container_client(). Credential = key, or DefaultAzureCredential (RBAC) in real Azure.

column1: What is a Request Unit (RU)?
column2: The normalized cost currency of Cosmos DB operations (read of 1 KB item ≈ 1 RU). You provision RU/s; throttled requests get HTTP 429 and the SDK retries. Query RU charge is returned in response headers.

column1: How do indexing policies affect RU consumption in Cosmos DB?
column2: By default every property is indexed — writes cost more RU. Exclude un-queried paths ("path": "/path/*" in excludedPaths) to cut write RU; add composite indexes for multi-property ORDER BY/filter queries, which otherwise fail or scan.

column1: List the five Cosmos DB consistency levels, strongest to weakest.
column2: Strong → Bounded Staleness → Session → Consistent Prefix → Eventual. Session is the default and the common exam answer: read-your-own-writes within a session at 1× read RU cost (strong costs 2×).

column1: Exam scenario: global app, users must always read their own writes but lowest latency. Consistency level?
column2: Session consistency — guarantees read-your-writes for the writer's session without Strong's latency/RU penalty.

column1: Cosmos DB vector search: how are embeddings stored and queried?
column2: Store the embedding as an array property; define a vector embedding policy (path, dimensions, data type) and a vector index (flat, quantizedFlat, or diskANN). Query with VectorDistance(<path>, <queryVector>) + ORDER BY RANK.

column1: Cosmos DB vector index types — which for what size?
column2: flat: brute-force exact, tiny datasets. quantizedFlat: quantized, good up to ~50k vectors. diskANN: approximate nearest neighbor on SSD — the default choice for large-scale semantic search.

column1: What does the Cosmos DB change feed processor do and what does it need?
column2: Pushes new/updated items to your handler in near-real-time, per partition. Needs: a monitored container, a lease container (tracks per-partition progress/checkpoints), a delegate (handler), and a processor instance name. Deletes and updates-deduplication are NOT captured (only latest state per item).

column1: Exam scenario: "detect and handle new or updated items for downstream AI processing" in Cosmos DB?
column2: Change feed processor (pull model in SDK) — not polling with queries. Lease container maintains progress so restarts resume where they left off.

column1: How do you choose a Cosmos DB partition key?
column2: High cardinality, evenly distributed request volume, present in most queries' filters (cross-partition queries fan out and multiply RU). Item id + partition key uniquely identify an item.

column1: Azure Database for PostgreSQL — Flexible Server: what is it?
column2: The managed Postgres option used in this exam: you pick compute tier (Burstable/GeneralPurpose/MemoryOptimized), storage, and Postgres version; Microsoft handles patching/HA. Vector workloads use the pgvector extension (CREATE EXTENSION vector;).

column1: pgvector: column type and insert?
column2: embedding vector(1536) — dimension count fixed per column. Insert as a JSON-ish array string: INSERT INTO docs(content, embedding) VALUES ('x', '[0.1,0.2,...]').

column1: pgvector distance operators?
column2: <-> L2/Euclidean, <#> (negative) inner product, <=> cosine distance. Cosine (<=>) is the default exam answer for text embeddings.

column1: pgvector index types and trade-offs?
column2: HNSW: better query performance/recall, slower builds, more memory; tune m, ef_construction, query-time ef_search. IVFFlat: faster build, less memory, requires data to exist first; tune lists (build) and probes (query). HNSW is the modern default.

column1: How do you write a pgvector similarity search with a metadata filter (RAG pattern)?
column2: SELECT content FROM docs WHERE category = 'faq' ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT 5; — filter on metadata first, then rank by vector distance. Set the index's vector_ops to match the operator (vector_cosine_ops).

column1: Reduce pgvector compute overhead — what levers exist?
column2: Use an ANN index (HNSW/IVFFlat) instead of sequential scan; reduce dimensions (or use half-precision halfvec); raise ef_search/probes only as needed (higher = more recall, more compute); ensure index is actually used (check with EXPLAIN).

column1: Postgres indexing strategy basics the exam expects?
column2: B-tree for equality/range; composite index column order follows leftmost-prefix rule; index what you filter/join/ORDER BY; too many indexes slow writes. Validate with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

column1: Configure Postgres compute/memory for vector workloads — which settings matter?
column2: shared_buffers (cache ~25% RAM), work_mem (per-sort/hash memory), maintenance_work_mem (index builds — raise to speed HNSW/IVFFlat creation), and enough vCores for parallel workers. On Flexible Server these are server parameters.

column1: Connection optimization for Postgres on Azure?
column2: Connection pooling — reuse connections, keep them short-lived, or use the built-in PgBouncer (transaction pooling) on Flexible Server. Python: psycopg_pool. Avoid opening a connection per query (TLS + auth handshake is expensive).

column1: Exam scenario: RAG over support tickets, must respect tenant isolation per query?
column2: Store tenant_id as a column, filter WHERE tenant_id = $2 in the pgvector similarity query (metadata-filtered RAG). Don't retrieve-then-filter in app code (wasteful and leaky).

column1: Azure Managed Redis — what is it and which tier features matter here?
column2: Microsoft's Redis offering (Redis Enterprise-based). For the exam: standard cache ops plus RediSearch vector similarity on supporting tiers — Redis doubles as a low-latency vector store.

column1: Cache-aside (lazy loading) pattern in Redis?
column2: Read: try cache → miss → read DB → SET with TTL. Write: update DB first, then invalidate (delete) the cache key. This is the default pattern the exam expects.

column1: How do expiration and TTL work in Redis?
column2: SET key val EX 300 or EXPIRE key 300; inspect with TTL key (-1 = no expiry, -2 = gone). Expired keys are removed lazily (on access) and actively (background sampling).

column1: Cache invalidation strategies to name-drop?
column2: TTL expiry (time-based), explicit delete on write (write-through invalidation), versioning key names (e.g. user:42:v3), and pub/sub invalidation messages across app instances. "There are only two hard things…" — the exam wants TTL + delete-on-write.

column1: Redis eviction policies — which ones matter?
column2: When maxmemory is hit: noeviction (errors on write), allkeys-lru (evict least-recently-used key overall — typical cache choice), volatile-lru (evict only keys with TTL set). A cache should use an allkeys-* policy, not noeviction.

column1: Redis vector search: index and query commands?
column2: FT.CREATE idx ON HASH|JSON SCHEMA embedding VECTOR HNSW 6 TYPE FLOAT32 DIM 1536 DISTANCE_METRIC COSINE, then FT.SEARCH idx "*=>[KNN 5 @embedding $vec]" PARAMS 2 vec <blob> DIALECT 2. RediSearch module required.

column1: Exam scenario: sub-millisecond semantic cache for LLM responses?
column2: Redis vector index: embed the incoming prompt, KNN-search cached prompt embeddings with a similarity threshold, return the cached completion on hit — semantic caching.

column1: Data domain — which service when? Cosmos vs Postgres vs Redis?
column2: Cosmos DB: globally distributed NoSQL, change feed, tunable consistency. Postgres: relational schema + pgvector, SQL, strong consistency, RAG with metadata filters. Redis: hot cache + low-latency vector search, ephemeral-friendly.

column1: Service Bus queue vs topic/subscription?
column2: Queue: point-to-point, competing consumers, one receiver gets each message. Topic: publish/subscribe — multiple subscriptions each get a copy, filtered per subscription.

column1: Service Bus receive modes?
column2: PeekLock (default): message locked, not deleted; you complete() on success — if the lock expires or you abandon, it's redelivered. ReceiveAndDelete: removed immediately — fastest, at-most-once, no recovery from processing failure.

column1: When does a message land in the Service Bus dead-letter queue?
column2: MaxDeliveryCount exceeded (repeated processing failure), message TTL expired (dead-lettering on message expiration enabled), filter evaluation exception, or explicit dead_letter() by the receiver. Inspect the DLQ for poison messages — it requires explicit reading.

column1: Exam scenario: intermittent downstream failures poison a queue — design?
column2: PeekLock with retry + MaxDeliveryCount; after N attempts the message dead-letters. A separate process reviews the DLQ (fix + resubmit). Don't lose messages with ReceiveAndDelete.

column1: Service Bus topic filters — the two types?
column2: SQL filters: SQL-92-ish expressions on message properties (priority = 'high'). Correlation filters: exact-match on properties, more efficient. Default is the 1=1 TrueFilter (everything matches).

column1: What are Service Bus sessions for?
column2: Ordered/groups processing: messages with the same session_id are received by one consumer at a time (session lock), preserving FIFO per session. Required for partitioned ordered workflows.

column1: Service Bus message essentials?
column2: Body + application properties (metadata for filters), message_id (duplicate detection), session_id, TTL (time_to_live), scheduled enqueue time (delayed delivery). Max size: 256 KB standard / 1 MB premium... verify current tier limits in docs.

column1: Python SDK: send and receive a Service Bus message?
column2: ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(cs) → get_queue_sender(q) / get_queue_receiver(q); sender.send_messages(ServiceBusMessage("body")); receiver: for msg in receiver: ... receiver.complete_message(msg).

column1: Event Grid: the core concepts?
column2: Event (what happened) → topic (where publishers send) → event subscription (routing config with filters) → event handler (the consumer: Function, webhook, queue...). Push model — Event Grid pushes to handlers.

column1: Event Grid filtering options?
column2: Subject filters (begins-with/ends-with on subject), event-type filters, and advanced filters on data payload fields (NumberGreaterThan, StringIn, etc.). Filters reduce noise and cost vs filtering in the handler.

column1: Event Grid delivery retry behavior?
column2: Push delivery with automatic retry on failure — exponential backoff, roughly 24 hours / 30 attempts by default (configurable per subscription: maxDeliveryAttempts, eventTimeToLive). After exhaustion → dead-letter to a storage container if configured.

column1: Exam scenario: "custom business events from your app, fan-out to multiple subscribers, filter by payload"?
column2: Custom Event Grid topic; publish EventGridEvent/CloudEvent payloads; subscriptions with subject/advanced filters per handler. Event Grid ≠ Service Bus: events are lightweight facts ("blob created"), not commands with sessions/DLQ semantics.

column1: Event Grid vs Service Bus — the classic discriminator?
column2: Event Grid: reactive, near-real-time "something happened" notifications, push, at-least-once with retries, huge fan-out. Service Bus: message brokering — commands/queues, pull, competing consumers, sessions, DLQ, ordering.

column1: Azure Functions: trigger vs binding?
column2: Exactly one trigger per function (what invokes it: HTTP, Timer, ServiceBus...). Bindings are declarative input/output connections (read a blob, write a queue message) without SDK boilerplate. Python v2 model: decorators (@app.route, @app.service_bus_queue_trigger).

column1: HTTP trigger authorization levels?
column2: anonymous (no key), function (function or host key), admin (master key). Keys passed as ?code= or x-functions-key header.

column1: Timer trigger schedule format?
column2: NCRONTAB with 6 fields (includes seconds): {second} {minute} {hour} {day} {month} {day-of-week}. 0 */5 * * * * = every 5 minutes. Times in UTC by default; WEBSITE_TIME_ZONE can change it.

column1: Functions hosting plans — pick by requirement?
column2: Consumption: scale-to-zero, pay-per-execution, cold start. Premium (Flex Consumption): pre-warmed instances, VNet, no cold start. Dedicated/Container Apps: run on your own compute/containers, custom images. Cold start avoidance → Premium.

column1: Configure and deploy a function app?
column2: Local: func init + func new, settings in local.settings.json (never commit secrets); app settings live in the function app in Azure. Deploy: func azure functionapp publish <name> (zip deploy) or a container image.

column1: host.json vs local.settings.json?
column2: host.json: runtime behavior — logging, retries, concurrency, binding-specific config (applies in Azure too). local.settings.json: local-only app settings/connection strings; in Azure these become App Settings/Key Vault references.

column1: Exam scenario: Function must start on a Service Bus topic message and write results to Cosmos DB?
column2: ServiceBus topic trigger (subscription name + connection setting) + Cosmos DB output binding. The trigger/binding pair removes custom polling and SDK write code.

column1: # ---------- DOMAIN: ops — secure, monitor, troubleshoot (20-25%) ----------
What does Azure Key Vault store?
column2: Secrets (connection strings, passwords), keys (RSA/EC, crypto ops in-HSM on premium), and certificates (with lifecycle management). Everything versioned: each set creates a new version under the same name.

column1: Key Vault secret rotation — how does it work?
column2: Rotation = create a new secret version and point consumers at it; because consumers read by name via SDK or Key Vault references, updating the value is enough — no app redeploy. Keys additionally support rotation policies (auto-rotate after N days).

column1: Two authorization models for Key Vault?
column2: Azure RBAC (recommended; roles like Key Vault Secrets Officer/Reader, uniform with the rest of Azure) vs legacy access policies (per-vault permission lists). New solutions → RBAC.

column1: Key Vault soft-delete and purge protection?
column2: Soft-delete (on by default): deleted objects recoverable for a retention period (default 90 days). Purge protection: even privileged users can't permanently delete before retention ends. Purging a vault with purge protection = impossible until expiry.

column1: Python: retrieve a secret from Key Vault?
column2: SecretClient(vault_url, credential) from azure-keyvault-secrets → get_secret("name") → .value. In real Azure, credential = DefaultAzureCredential (Managed Identity). On floci-az you use the emulator endpoint + fixed dev credentials (see ADR-0001).

column1: Azure App Configuration — what belongs there vs Key Vault?
column2: App Configuration: non-secret settings — feature flags, per-environment config (use labels like dev/prod). Secrets stay in Key Vault; App Configuration stores Key Vault references to compose both.

column1: How do live configuration refreshes work with App Configuration?
column2: The provider caches settings; you designate a sentinel key — bump it to signal change. App refreshes only when the sentinel changes (avoids reloading on every key change), with a refresh-interval cache to bound latency.

column1: Feature flags in App Configuration?
column2: Feature management: flags stored under .appconfig.featureflag/, evaluated per request with filters (percentage rollout, targeting users/groups, time window). Flip behavior without redeploying.

column1: Exam scenario: settings must differ per environment and secrets must never be in config stores?
column2: App Configuration with labels per environment; secret-valued entries as Key Vault references; app uses one client that resolves both transparently.

column1: OpenTelemetry: the three core trace concepts?
column2: Trace: the whole operation end-to-end (one trace_id). Span: one unit of work (operation name, start/end, status). Attributes/events: key-value metadata and timestamped notes on a span.

column1: How does distributed context propagation work in OpenTelemetry?
column2: The trace context (traceparent header: trace-id, parent span-id, flags) is injected into outgoing HTTP/messaging calls and extracted by the receiver, so spans from different services join one trace. W3C Trace Context is the standard.

column1: Minimal Python OTel setup for tracing?
column2: Create a TracerProvider, add a SpanProcessor with an exporter (OTLP HTTP to a collector/Jaeger, or Azure Monitor distro for App Insights), get a tracer, and wrap work in with tracer.start_as_current_span("op"):. Instrumentation libraries auto-trace requests/httpx/redis etc.

column1: Exam scenario: a request crosses Function → Service Bus → worker, and you must see it as one operation?
column2: OpenTelemetry at each hop with context propagation (trace context travels in message application properties). In real Azure: export to Application Insights for the end-to-end transaction view. Locally: OTLP → Jaeger.

column1: Azure Monitor vs Application Insights vs Log Analytics?
column2: Application Insights = APM for apps (traces, requests, dependencies) — an OpenTelemetry destination. Log Analytics = the KQL queryable log store underneath. Azure Monitor = the umbrella service (metrics, logs, alerts) tying them together.

column1: What is KQL and where does it run?
column2: Kusto Query Language — read-only queries over Log Analytics / Azure Monitor / ADX tables. Pipe-shaped: Table | where ... | summarize ... | render. The exam asks you to write it, not just read it.

column1: KQL: filter and shape rows?
column2: where (filter — use ==, contains, ago(1h)), project (choose columns), extend (compute new columns), distinct, take/limit. Put the most selective where first for performance.

column1: KQL: aggregate and time-bin?
column2: summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), Level — bin() floors timestamps to buckets; common aggregations: count(), count_distinct(), avg(), percentile(x, 95). Then render timechart to visualize.

column1: KQL: combine tables?
column2: join kind=inner (OtherTable) on Key; union appends tables; let defines reusable variables/subqueries. mv-expand unnests dynamic arrays.

column1: Write a KQL query: exceptions in the last 24h, grouped by type, top 10.
column2: exceptions | where timestamp > ago(24h) | summarize count() by type | top 10 by count_ desc

column1: Exam scenario: find the slowest dependency calls of an app this week?
column2: dependencies | where timestamp > ago(7d) | summarize p95=percentile(duration, 95) by target, name | order by p95 desc — App Insights dependencies table holds outbound calls.

column1: Order of magnitude: exam weights?
column2: Data management 25–30% (heaviest); containers, integration, and secure/monitor/troubleshoot each 20–25%. Passing score 700/1000; ~54–58 questions in 120 min.

column1: Reported exam format (Reddit consensus, Aug 2026)?
column2: ~5 case-study questions, ~49 mixed (MCQ, dropdown/select-value, ordering), then ~4 Yes/No questions in a no-return section (no review after clicking Next). MS Learn is browsable during the exam. No live lab reported.

column1: # ---------- extra batch: containers ----------
ACR SKU tiers — which features gate on Premium?
column2: Basic/Standard/Premium. Premium unlocks geo-replication, private endpoints, and content trust. Geo-replication = images replicated to multiple regions, pulls served locally.

column1: How do you authenticate to ACR to pull/push?
column2: az acr login -n <registry> (docker login via AAD token) for dev; for AKS use az aks create --attach-acr (grants the kubelet AcrPull role); for services use a managed identity or admin/service-principal credentials.

column1: Container Apps ingress — what can you configure?
column2: External vs internal visibility, target port, transport (HTTP/TCP), and traffic weights across revisions. Internal-only apps are reachable just inside the environment — right answer for backend workers.

column1: How are secrets handled in Container Apps?
column2: Stored as secrets on the app (az containerapp secret set), referenced by env vars (secretref:) — never in plain env vars. Rotation = update secret; new revision picks it up.

column1: Command to split traffic between Container Apps revisions?
column2: az containerapp ingress traffic set -n <app> -g <rg> --revision-weight latest=80 previous=20 — requires multiple revision mode.

column1: Kubernetes Service types — ClusterIP vs NodePort vs LoadBalancer?
column2: ClusterIP (default): cluster-internal only. NodePort: exposes a static port on every node. LoadBalancer: provisions a cloud LB with a public IP — the typical AKS answer for exposing a service externally.

column1: ConfigMap vs Secret in Kubernetes?
column2: Both inject config into Pods (env vars or mounted files). ConfigMap = plain config; Secret = base64-encoded sensitive values (encrypt at rest, RBAC-restricted). Secrets are not encryption by themselves.

column1: How do you roll out and roll back a Deployment?
column2: kubectl apply triggers a rolling update; kubectl rollout status deployment/x watches it; kubectl rollout undo deployment/x reverts to the previous ReplicaSet. Rolling update honors maxSurge/maxUnavailable.

column1: What do AKS node pools separate?
column2: Groups of nodes with same VM size/config: the required system pool (runs kube-system pods) vs user pools for your workloads (can scale to zero, spot instances, GPU sizes).

column1: How do you debug a running container on AKS interactively?
column2: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /bin/sh; kubectl port-forward <pod> 8080:80 for local access to a Pod port; kubectl debug for ephemeral containers.

column1: Exam scenario: container needs patching rebuilt automatically whenever its base image updates?
column2: ACR Task with a base image trigger — ACR tracks base image updates and rebuilds your image automatically.

column1: Cosmos DB: point read vs query — RU impact?
column2: A point read (id + partition key) costs ~1 RU for 1 KB — the cheapest operation. Queries consume multiple RUs and can fan out cross-partition; prefer point reads and partition-scoped queries.

column1: Cosmos DB time-to-live?
column2: Container-level defaultTimeToLive (seconds) with optional per-item ttl override; expired items are deleted automatically without consuming delete RUs. Useful for ephemeral AI session state.

column1: Parameterized Cosmos DB query in Python?
column2: container.query_items(query="SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.tenant=@t", parameters=[{"name":"@t","value":tid}], partition_key=tid) — always parameterize (injection-safe) and pass partition_key when possible.

column1: Cosmos DB change feed via Azure Functions?
column2: The Cosmos DB trigger is a change-feed processor managed by the Functions runtime (leases container required) — simplest way to react to inserts/updates without hosting the processor yourself.

column1: Why is Strong consistency twice as expensive for reads in Cosmos DB?
column2: Reads must be served/confirmed by a quorum of replicas, consuming ~2× the RUs of weaker levels — plus higher latency. That's why Session is the default.

column1: Enabling pgvector on Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server?
column2: Allow-list the extension via the azure.extensions server parameter (VECTOR), then CREATE EXTENSION vector; in your database.

column1: IVFFlat gotcha the exam loves?
column2: Build the index after the table is populated — IVFFlat clusters existing rows into lists; an index built on an empty table won't cover later inserts well (recall degrades). HNSW has no such requirement.

column1: How do you confirm Postgres actually uses your vector index?
column2: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) SELECT ... — look for an Index Scan using the HNSW/IVFFlat index. A Seq Scan means the index was skipped (table too small, probes/ef_search unset, or ops-class mismatch).

column1: halfvec in pgvector — why use it?
column2: halfvec stores embeddings as 2-byte floats — halves memory and index size at slight precision cost, letting larger vector sets stay in memory (shared_buffers) for low latency.

column1: psycopg connection to Azure Postgres — what settings matter?
column2: psycopg.connect("host=... dbname=... user=... password=... sslmode=require") — Azure Postgres requires TLS (sslmode=require); use psycopg_pool for pooling.

column1: Redis: SET with NX/XX flags?
column2: SET key val NX — set only if not exists (distributed lock primitive); XX — set only if it exists. Combined with EX for lock expiry.

column1: How do you batch Redis commands efficiently?
column2: Pipelining (redis-py pipe = r.pipeline()): send multiple commands in one round trip — the main throughput lever vs one RTT per command.

column1: Redis key naming convention?
column2: Readable, colon-separated: object-type:id:field (user:42:name, session:abc). Keeps keys scannable and avoids collisions across features.

column1: redis-py connection to Azure Managed Redis?
column2: redis.Redis(host=..., port=10000, password=<access-key>, ssl=True) — Azure Managed Redis uses TLS and access-key (or Entra) auth; port 10000 is the Enterprise-style default.

column1: Why does a RediSearch KNN query need DIALECT 2+?
column2: Vector KNN syntax (*=>[KNN ...]) was introduced in query dialect 2 — without DIALECT 2 the query parser rejects or misinterprets it.

column1: Exam scenario: cache LLM embeddings and find the 5 most similar in under 5 ms?
column2: Managed Redis + RediSearch HNSW vector index; KNN query with DIALECT 2; keep the index in memory — no disk round trips.

column1: # ---------- extra batch: integration ----------
Service Bus message settlement operations?
column2: complete (done, remove), abandon (release back for redelivery), dead_letter (move to DLQ with reason), defer (park it; retrieve later by sequence number — for out-of-order processing).

column1: Service Bus duplicate detection?
column2: Enable on the queue/topic: within a time window, a second message with the same message_id is discarded — gives at-most-once publishing despite sender retries.

column1: How do you raise Service Bus receive throughput?
column2: Enable prefetch (receiver buffers messages locally), receive in batches, and scale out competing consumers — partitioned entities also parallelize.

column1: Service Bus auto-forwarding?
column2: Chain entities: messages landing in a queue/subscription are automatically forwarded to another queue/topic (e.g., DLQ of one entity → processing queue). Max hop rules apply; destination must exist.

column1: Event Grid event schemas?
column2: EventGridEvent (Azure-native schema: topic, subject, eventType, eventTime, data) and CloudEvents v1.0 (CNCF standard: source, type, subject, data). Pick CloudEvents for portability.

column1: Event Grid webhook endpoint validation?
column2: On subscription creation Event Grid sends a SubscriptionValidationEvent; your webhook must echo the validationCode to prove ownership before events flow.

column1: Event Grid system topics vs custom topics vs domains?
column2: System topics: Azure service events (Blob created...). Custom topics: your app's own events. Domains: many related topics managed as one — multi-tenant fan-out.

column1: Azure Functions Python v2 programming model?
column2: Decorators in function_app.py (app = func.FunctionApp(), @app.function_name, @app.route, @app.service_bus_queue_trigger) — replaces the v1 function.json files.

column1: How do you avoid cold start in Functions?
column2: Use a Premium/Flex Consumption plan with pre-warmed instances, or run on Container Apps/Dedicated. On Consumption you accept cold starts after idle scale-to-zero.

column1: Function retry policy for transient failures?
column2: Configure in host.json: strategy exponentialBackoff or fixedDelay, maxRetryCount, delay intervals — applies per trigger before messages dead-letter.

column1: Service Bus trigger message completion behavior in Functions?
column2: By default the runtime auto-completes the message when the function succeeds and abandons it on failure (lock released → redelivery). Control with autoCompleteMessages in host.json or settle manually via the receive actions.

column1: Exam scenario: hundreds of tenants each need isolated event streams from one app?
column2: Event Grid domain — one domain, a topic per tenant, per-topic subscriptions and access control.

column1: Key Vault object URI format?
column2: https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/<secrets|keys|certificates>/<name>[/<version>] — omitting the version gets the latest.

column1: How do you lock down Key Vault network access?
column2: Disable public access and use private endpoints, or firewall-allow selected VNets/IPs. Combine with RBAC — network restriction alone isn't authorization.

column1: How do you roll back an App Configuration change safely?
column2: Take a snapshot before risky changes (immutable point-in-time view) and restore from it; or revert the specific key-value/label.

column1: OpenTelemetry span kinds?
column2: server (handles a request), client (makes an outbound call), internal (in-process), producer/consumer (messaging). Kinds let backends render dependency direction correctly.

column1: OpenTelemetry sampling strategies?
column2: parentbased_always_on (everything, honors parent decision) vs traceidratio (sample a fraction, e.g. 0.1). Production high-volume → ratio sampling; exam answers favor "sample but keep errors".

column1: Metrics vs logs in Azure Monitor?
column2: Metrics: lightweight numeric time series, near-real-time, cheap, pre-aggregated. Logs: rich structured records (traces, requests, exceptions) in Log Analytics, queried with KQL, higher latency/cost. Alert fast on metrics, diagnose with logs.

column1: KQL: has vs contains?
column2: has matches whole indexed terms (fast) — "error" won't match "terror"... actually it matches term boundaries; contains does substring matching (slower). Prefer has for term searches.

column1: KQL: turn raw text into columns?
column2: parse (positional patterns) or extract(regex, captureGroup, source); extend with todatetime()/toint() to cast.

column1: KQL: per-user request counts in the last hour?
column2: requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) | summarize count() by user_Id | order by count_ desc

column1: Exam scenario: one bad deployment caused a latency spike — how do you prove it?
column2: KQL over requests: summarize avg(duration) by bin(timestamp, 5m), cloud_RoleName, then render timechart — the step change aligns with deploy time; correlate via OTel trace attributes carrying the version.

column1: Exam scenario: rotate a database password used by 12 apps with zero redeploys?
column2: Store it as a Key Vault secret; apps read via Key Vault references / SDK at runtime. Rotate = create new secret version (and update the DB side); apps pick it up on next read/refresh.

column1: Exam scenario: secrets in a Functions app on floci-az vs real Azure — what's different?
column2: floci-az uses fixed Azurite-style dev credentials/connection strings (no Entra/Managed Identity). In real Azure you'd use DefaultAzureCredential + Managed Identity with Key Vault RBAC — know the pattern even though you can't run it locally (see ADR-0001).

column1: How does kubectl get credentials for an AKS cluster?
column2: az aks get-credentials -g <rg> -n <cluster> — merges the cluster's kubeconfig into ~/.kube/config (uses Azure RBAC/admin creds).

column1: Rolling update knobs maxSurge and maxUnavailable?
column2: maxSurge: how many Pods above desired may exist during a rollout; maxUnavailable: how many may be down. Both can be counts or percentages. Defaults 25%/25%.

column1: Cordon vs drain a node?
column2: cordon marks the node unschedulable (existing Pods stay). drain cordons and evicts Pods (respecting PodDisruptionBudgets) — used before maintenance.

column1: Fastest way to deploy source code to Container Apps in one command?
column2: az containerapp up --source . — builds (via ACR/OLC) and deploys an app + environment scaffolding. Great for demos; CI uses ACR Tasks + az containerapp update.

column1: Cosmos DB vector embedding policy — what does it declare?
column2: Per vector path: the dimensions (must match your model, e.g. 1536), the data type (float32), and the distance function (cosine). Required before vector indexes/queries work on that path.

column1: When is quantizedFlat the right Cosmos DB vector index?
column2: Small-to-medium datasets (tens of thousands of vectors) where exact flat scan is too slow but diskANN is overkill; it quantizes vectors for speed with slight recall loss.

column1: Change feed pull model vs the Functions Cosmos DB trigger?
column2: Same change feed underneath. Pull model (query_items_change_feed) = you host the loop and checkpointing; the Functions trigger = runtime hosts the processor (lease container still required). Pick the trigger for simple reactions.

column1: Postgres work_mem gotcha?
column2: It's per sort/hash operation, not per connection — a complex query can use multiples; set it too high and concurrent queries exhaust memory.

column1: Azure Managed Redis connection security?
column2: TLS-only by default (Enterprise-style port 10000); clients must use ssl=True — a plain-text client is the classic "can't connect" cause.

column1: Exam scenario: globally distributed AI app, needs insert/update reactions across regions?
column2: Cosmos DB — multi-region writes/reads plus the change feed; Postgres Flexible Server is single-region-primary and Redis is a cache, not the system of record.

column1: Service Bus prefetch — what and why?
column2: Receiver-side buffering of messages ahead of processing: raises throughput by cutting round trips; interacts with lock duration (prefetched locks tick), so don't prefetch deep with slow handlers.

column1: How do you schedule a Service Bus message for future delivery?
column2: Set scheduled_enqueue_time (UTC) when sending — the message appears in the queue only at that time; cancel via its sequence number.

column1: Event Grid event size limit?
column2: Events up to 1 MB are supported; payloads are metered in 64 KB chunks. Bigger payloads → claim-check pattern (event carries a blob URL).

column1: Functions host.json retry strategies?
column2: fixedDelay (constant wait) vs exponentialBackoff (growing wait between min/max) with maxRetryCount — applies per trigger before messages dead-letter.

column1: Key Vault key rotation policy details?
column2: Configure per key: automatic rotation after N days, plus near-expiry notifications published via Event Grid (system topic) — a favorite crossover exam fact.

column1: Key Vault certificates — what lifecycle feature is managed?
column2: Auto-renewal with integrated CAs (e.g. DigiCert/GlobalSign): contacts, issuers, and renewal policy live on the cert; KV rotates and stores the new version automatically.

column1: OpenTelemetry baggage vs span attributes?
column2: Attributes annotate one span; baggage is key-values propagated across service boundaries with the trace context (e.g. tenant id available to every downstream span).

column1: KQL: what is the default name of a summarize count column, and how do you rename it?
column2: count_ — rename inline: summarize n=count() by .... Use let for reusable subqueries/variables above the pipe chain.

column1: A Cosmos DB document's partition key is changed — what appears in the change feed?
column2: An insert of the new item only. A PK change is a delete + re-insert, and the feed never captures deletes — so only the insert surfaces.

column1: Cache runs volatile-ttl but most keys were SET without a TTL — what happens under memory pressure?
column2: evicted_keys stays ~0 and writes fail with OOM errors: volatile-ttl (like all volatile-* policies) only evicts keys that have a TTL; everything else is unevictable. A general cache wants allkeys-lru.

column1: Why can't an HTTP scaling rule react to Service Bus backlog in Container Apps?
column2: The HTTP scaler counts concurrent HTTP requests only — queue depth is invisible to it. Queue-driven scale-to-zero needs the KEDA azure-servicebus scaler with minReplicas: 0.
